correctness.rationale: A generic one-parameter subgroup of the scroll torus has pairwise distinct weights on all ambient coordinate monomials, so projective fixed points are coordinate axes. Projection to the i-th directrix block takes every scroll-cone point to either zero or a pure degree-d_i binary power; conversely that directrix is contained in the scroll. Thus the scroll border rank of x_{i,j} equals the rational-normal-curve border rank of s^(d_i-j)t^j. For q=min(j,d_i-j), the q-th catalecticant has rank q+1, giving the lower bound, while the q-th finite difference of a pure power gives a border decomposition with q+1 summands. Therefore fixed membership is exactly q+1<=r, yielding min(d_i+1,2r) points in block i. Euler localization then gives the formula. The packaged checker independently verifies the catalecticant ranks, finite-difference identities, and fixed-coordinate counts over a broad finite regression range.

value.rationale: Rational normal scrolls are classical varieties of minimal degree whose higher secants exhibit nontrivial determinantal equations and defectivity. The theorem computes a global topological invariant for every secant level and every smooth splitting type in one closed formula. It reveals a structural decomposition invisible in the usual dimension and degree theory: each directrix contributes independently, at a rate of exactly two Euler units per rank step until saturation. This also identifies precisely when the Euler characteristic reaches the ambient value, regardless of whether the secant variety has already filled the ambient space. The result is therefore an all-family structural statement rather than a routine small-rank calculation.
